rendered_html: 📔 Regulatory Bulletin — 28 August 2026 (Daily) Executive Summary • 🟡 HKMA and three financial regulators announced the first GenA.I. Sandbox++ cohort, providing a controlled, early-supervisory-engagement route for selected agentic-AI use cases across onboarding, payments and customer interactions. • The initiative is not a new binding requirement; it nevertheless signals a near-term market and supervisory-development path for comparable AI-enabled banking journeys, where accountability, customer outcomes and technology-partner dependencies warrant management attention. • Technical trials are due to commence later in 2026, without a specific source-stated date; participating or comparable use cases should have an approved applicability decision and proportionate governance evidence. Hong Kong 🟡 First cohort of GenA.I. Sandbox++ 🇭🇰 Item ID: item-20260827-hkma-press-74e83c55f1 ⏰ Deadline: Technical trials commence later in 2026; no specific date stated. Products: Digital banking; SME onboarding; Payments The HKMA, SFC, IA and MPFA announced the first GenA.I. Sandbox++ cohort: 36 selected use cases from nearly 100 proposals, involving 30 financial institutions and 27 technology partners. The controlled testing covers agentic-AI applications across end-to-end customer onboarding, payments, insurance claims and customer interactions, with Cyberport’s platform hosting technical trials later in 2026. This is a testing initiative with early supervisory engagement, not a rule, direction or industry-wide obligation; the release does not identify participating authorised institutions or specify control standards, approval requirements or implementation dates. For participating or comparable planned digital journeys, a proportionate commercial and risk preparation step is to identify applicability and consider governance, human oversight, customer communications, data flows, vendor diligence, testing and monitoring evidence. Source: First cohort of GenA.I. Sandbox++ Mainland/GBA No validated current-run items. SG/UK/GLOBAL Benchmark Comparable overseas developments and commercial/control benchmarks. They do not establish Hong Kong requirements. No validated current-run items. Watch List • Monitor whether the selected Sandbox++ use cases involve authorised institutions and whether the technical trials produce later HKMA or SFC expectations; neither point is stated in the announcement.
